doc.name: A — lighting fixtures catalogue, miniature diorama, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: opal glass pendant lamp
Category: lighting fixtures
Shot programme: miniature diorama
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium lighting fixtures product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the reflection duet in a miniature diorama treatment.

SUBJECT. A opal glass pendant lamp. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Product and its reflection on a polished plane, symmetric split. Shoot on a 58mm vintage double-gauss at f/8, framing for deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with hard side light with 80 percent of the frame falling into shadow. Stage the product on or against crushed velvet, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
